_comment: The machine-readable index for one docs directory. Copy this file, replace
every REPLACE, delete every block the project does not need, and delete this
_comment key. JSON has no comments, so this is the only place they live.
DIVISION OF LABOUR — the rule that keeps the two artifacts from drifting:
the HTML owns the narrative — purpose lines, prose, reads/persists/emits;
this file owns identity, contracts, invariants, decisions and views.
Nothing is declared in both. In particular there are no reads/writes here:
check_docs.py parses those out of the map's own chips, so the map stays the
single place a flow is described.
title: REPLACE — the system or pipeline name a reader would recognise
//status: This one field decides whether the checker compares the docs against code and
data at all. A design that is not implemented has no stage enum to read and no
data directory to glob, so those checks are skipped and the run says so.
Getting this wrong in either direction is expensive: 'built' on a design gives
a wall of errors that all mean 'not implemented yet', which is how a checker
gets ignored; 'proposed' on shipped code silently switches off the only checks
//system: The level-0 context page, if there is one. Omit for a single pipeline.
//component_map: The structural page: components, what each owns, and the channels between
them. Omit it for a system with one component or no supervision structure —
there is nothing to map that the pipeline map does not already say.
Checked exactly like `map`: every entry in `components` needs a card on it,
//index: The landing page that routes a reader to the right map. Every page named in
this file must be linked from it, and a page sitting in the directory that
the index does not link is reported — that is how a drill-down written last
week goes unread. Omit the key if there is only one page to route to.
//stage_source: `file · symbol` — the authoritative stage list in the CODE, in the same
grammar as a .ref chip. An enum whose members carry string values, or a
Point it at the ENUM, not at something derived from the enum: a comprehension
like `STAGES = [s.value for s in StageName]` holds no literals to read, and the
checker will tell you so rather than guess.
This is the single highest-value line in the file — it is what makes a renamed
or reordered stage fail a check instead of rotting.
//views: Named readings of the one model. A stage lists the views it belongs to; the
map's view bar filters to one at a time. Add a view when a real audience keeps
needing a subset — not one per stage group.
//stages: The spine, in execution order. Per stage:
id          the number on the map's rail. Must match a card.
name        the stage's real name in the codebase. A reader greps it.
code_names  which stage_source members this card covers. Defaults to [name].
Use [] for a verb outside the run pipeline (a setup command), and
a list of two when one card covers two members that always run
together. Flattened in order, these must equal the code's list.
drilldown   the level-2 page, if one exists. Coverage is reported, not required.
views       which views this stage appears in.
not         responsibilities this stage explicitly does NOT take on. The map
has no place for these and they are where scope creep lands, so
they live here. Set "no_not": true to declare there are none.
invariants  claims that must hold for the stage to be correct, written so a
reader can check the code against them. "no_invariants": true to
adr         decision records that shaped it, by leading id.
NOTE there is deliberately no `purpose` here: that is the map's `.goal` line,
and giving it two homes would let one of them drift.

stages.name: REPLACE-first-stage
not: REPLACE — the neighbouring concern a reader would assume lives here
invariants: REPLACE — a claim a reader can check the code against

//components: The owners, for the component map. A stage is a step in a sequence; a
component is a thing that owns a responsibility, and the two lists are not
the same shape — one process often spans several stages. Per component:
id          the number on the component map's rail. Must match a card.
name        what it is called in the system. A reader greps it.
external    INSTEAD of name, the id of an already-declared external this
card presents. Use it when a system is a component to a reader
and an external to the boundary page — it stays declared once.
kind        deterministic | agentic | mixed | store | external. Informational;
the card's own tags are what a reader sees.
not         responsibilities it is structurally prevented from taking on.
This is the field that makes the page worth writing.
invariants  claims that must hold for the component to be correct.
adr         decision records that shaped it, by leading id.
There is deliberately no `drilldown` here: a component's deeper page is a
STAGE page, on the other axis, and linking it belongs in the card's HTML.

components.name: REPLACE — e.g. the supervisor
not: REPLACE — the responsibility a reader would assume it holds and it does not
invariants: REPLACE — a claim a reader can check the code against

//channels: The edges of the component map: what travels, and between whom. Same role
`edges` plays for the level-0 page — the machine-readable model, not the
prose. The page's own channels table is where a reader meets them, and what
breaks when one goes silent belongs there, not here.
from / to   a component id or an external id.
carries     the payload, in the system's own words. Required — a channel
with no payload named is a line on a diagram.
//externals: Systems outside the boundary, for the level-0 page. These have no card of
their own, so their purpose is declared here and the checker requires it.
An external MAY also appear as a component card via `external` above — that
is one declaration presented twice, not two declarations.

externals.title: REPLACE — e.g. a model API
externals.purpose: REPLACE — what it is for here, and what breaks without it.

//edges: Only the relationships the numbered rail CANNOT express: a side channel every
stage uses (telemetry, a run archive), or a link to an external system. Do not
restate stage N → stage N+1 — the order already says that.
Endpoints must be a stage id or an external id.
//data_globs: Where the real artifacts live, relative to --source-root. Every file found
here must be claimed by some card's persists/writes chips, or listed in
`ignore`. This is how a sidecar nobody documented surfaces.
//contracts: The shape of each durable artifact at a stage boundary — what the next stage
is entitled to assume. Keyed by the filename as the map writes it.
sample     glob for real files to check against, relative to --source-root.
ANCHOR IT: a loose `chapter-*.sections.json` also matches
check then fails against the wrong file.
required   keys that must be present in EVERY record of every sample.
optional   keys that may be absent. Anything present and undeclared warns.
invariants prose claims. Printed as a reminder, NOT machine-checked — the
checker says so on every run so nobody mistakes them for verified.

invariants: REPLACE — a claim about the shape that no key check can see

//configuration: Values that were calibrated rather than chosen, and that other things now
depend on. Declared here so a reader can find every load-bearing number in
one place instead of grepping prose.
//open_questions: Decisions not yet made, and decisions deliberately deferred. Say which —
'deferred until retrieval is evaluated' is a different state from 'nobody has
decided', and only one of them is a problem.
open_questions: REPLACE — an undecided or deliberately deferred question
